Subject: Acme Retail - Technical deep-dive recap & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Below is a concise recap of the technical items we covered, the key pain points you called out, and proposed next steps. Please flag anything I missed or got wrong.

Summary of pain points / goals
- Latency spikes for conversational search (95th percentile often > 300ms for ~512 tokens) causing poor UX on peak traffic
- High per-token inference cost for heavy RAG workloads; want to get economic below $X per 1k tokens for core flows
- KV cache misses across sessions leading to repeated generation and higher latency
- Need private networking + SOC2 evidence for procurement

SLOs you indicated are required
- Target P95 latency: <= 150 ms for 512 tokens (interactive UI)
- Sustained throughput: ~120 reqs/sec during peak windows (with bursts to 200 reqs/sec)
- Availability target: 99.9% SLA for production endpoints

Model / workload constraints
- Primary model: LLM-XL-8B (we discussed quantized 4/8-bit variants) for best quality/latency balance
- Fallback: LLM-Medium-4B for lower-cost, high-concurrency tails
- Retrieval window: average context size ~3k tokens; typical response lengths 200-600 tokens

Deployment topology discussed
- Recommended: Dedicated capacity in US-West region (private VPC) behind smart routing
- Autoscale policy: baseline reserved pool sized for sustained 120 reqs/sec; burst layer for peaks
- KV prefix caching enabled per-session; warm cache for repeat users via sticky routing

Attachments shared in call
- acme_slo_matrix.xlsx (SLO worksheet)
- mutual_action_plan.pdf (timeline & owners)

Immediate next steps
1) Rishi (SE) to send a short technical deep-dive recap with proposed GPU sizing / architecture and a deployment diagram.
2) Acme to confirm security questionnaire items and provide a primary procurement contact (we have Priya on copy).
3) Schedule an architecture workshop (60-90m) to validate topology and run a small perf test on a sample prompt set.

If that looks right, I’ll follow up with calendar invites for the workshop and attach the MAP + SLO worksheet as a working doc.

Best,

Hi Alex / Priya — quick technical follow-up from our SE side (forwarding Marissa’s recap with details).

Key technical proposal (high-level)
- GPU sizing: For the LLM-XL-8B quantized (4-bit), we recommend 2x A10G (or equivalent T4-class) per serving shard for low-latency interactive flows. For peak throughput and burst capacity, we can add H100-backed shards for cost-insensitive batch work.
- Batching / concurrency: Target micro-batch sizes of 8-16 with continuous batching to keep P95 latency within target while maintaining GPU efficiency.
- KV cache strategy: Use session-affinity routing to warm KV cache; reserve a small fast-cache tier (in-memory on serving nodes) for the top 5% of hot prefixes. This cuts repeated retrieval overhead.
- Quantization: 4-bit int8/4 quantization for the 8B model keeps token cost low while hitting quality targets; we validated on your sample prompts with a <6% quality delta in our bench.
- Fallbacks: Configure automatic fallback to 4B variant for requests that exceed latency budget or when reserved capacity is constrained.

Estimated perf numbers (ballpark, to be validated in the workshop)
- 512-token gen, single request, P95: ~110-160 ms on A10G-class with continuous batching (micro-batch 8)
- Sustained throughput (per 2x A10G shard): ~80-100 reqs/sec; scale horizontally to meet 120 reqs/sec baseline

Suggested architecture (attached diagram)
- Private VPC in US-West with dedicated Redwood cluster
- Ingress -> Edge routing layer (TLS + mutual auth) -> Model service pool (quantized 8B primary, 4B fallback) -> KV cache layer + vector DB (customer-managed)

Action items we’ll bring to the architecture workshop
- Run a short perf test using your representative prompt set (we’ll provide a harness)
- Validate warm-cache policy and hit-rate targets
- Review SOC2 evidence and KMS integration steps (Neha will lead this)

Attachments: redwood_deployment_diagram.png (high-level topology), quick_test_harness.sh (link in Drive)

Proposed times for architecture workshop:
- Tue Oct 6, 11:00 AM PT / Wed Oct 7, 6:00 AM CET
- Wed Oct 7, 2:00 PM PT (alternate)

If any of these recommendations look off, tell me and we’ll adjust prior to the workshop. Happy to deep-dive on the quantization/latency tradeoffs.

Regards,
